# Amazon Keyspaces (for Apache Cassandra)

Manage Cassandra keyspaces, tables, and user-defined types locally, with opt-in Cassandra execution.

**Status: implemented subset.** Operation selection does not imply complete input or behavior parity.

| Contract | Current implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Service ID | `keyspaces` |
| Signing name | `cassandra` |
| Wire protocol | AWS JSON 1.0, Smithy RPC v2 CBOR |
| API version | `2022-02-10` |
| Scope | Account and region |
| Execution | Records / optional Docker |
| Selected operations | 17 of 19 in the pinned model |

## Implemented behavior

See the [implemented feature catalogue](catalogue.md#amazon-keyspaces-for-apache-cassandra) for this service's capabilities.

## Connect over CQL

Enable the runtime for local CQL access:

```yaml
storage:
  mode: persistent
  path: ./state
keyspaces:
  runtime: docker
```

The first keyspace in each account and Region starts a single `cassandra:5` container. The official Apache Cassandra
image provides both the native CQL protocol and the matching `cqlsh` client. Docker assigns an ephemeral
`127.0.0.1` port for container port 9042. Find the keyspace in `GET /_tinystack/resources` and read
`details.CqlEndpoint` after startup. For a new table, wait for `GetTable` to report `ACTIVE` before connecting.

```sh
cqlsh 127.0.0.1 <port>
```

Committed schema changes, including table, keyspace and type deletions, are applied in order with `docker exec … cqlsh`.
If Cassandra is unavailable or CQL fails, the head of the queue is retried and the resource inventory shows
`details.RuntimeError` while a resource in that scope remains. Manage schema through the Keyspaces API so that
Cassandra and the control plane agree. CQL reads and row writes go directly to Cassandra.

Shutdown removes the store's containers and keeps its named data volumes. Reusing the same persistent store
recovers the data and pending schema changes. Recreated containers may use a new port. Reset removes the store's
containers and volumes. A memory store has a new runtime owner after restart, so use persistent storage to retain CQL
data across TinyStack restarts. Keep Docker mode enabled when resetting a persistent store so TinyStack can remove its volumes.


## Limitations and future work

- Records mode has no CQL data plane. Docker uses stock Cassandra CQL and schema features without TLS, the Keyspaces SigV4 authentication plugin, IAM data-plane enforcement, or AWS endpoint discovery.
- Multi-Region replication is metadata only. Other Regions do not receive a copy, and the local Cassandra node uses a single replica. UpdateKeyspace can add Regions and enable client-side timestamps across existing tables. Removing Regions is unsupported.
- Capacity, customer-managed encryption, point-in-time recovery, and client-side timestamp settings do not configure the Docker engine. Cassandra supports per-write TTL and timestamps natively.
- RestoreTable, GetTableAutoScalingSettings, change data capture, replica overrides, and warm throughput are unsupported. DeleteKeyspace requires removing its tables and user-defined types first.
- Table and user-defined type field identifiers are limited to alphanumeric characters and underscores. Quoted type names preserve case within the supported identifier characters. The built-in keyspaces expose names and metadata. Their system tables are accessible only through Cassandra CQL where Cassandra provides them.

These gaps describe current boundaries and possible follow-up slices. The [roadmap](../roadmap/index.md)
separates proposed work from registered functionality; there are no promised release dates.

## Supported operations

The table is generated from the profile and pinned Smithy model. Routes show REST bindings or the standard
JSON/Query endpoint. RPC v2 CBOR uses its service/operation route, as described in
[protocol handling](../architecture/request-flow.md). Supported members are selected separately in the
[shape whitelist](https://github.com/amjadjibon/tinystack/blob/main/generator/model/profile.json); an enabled operation may reject unsupported options.

| Operation | HTTP binding |
| --- | --- |
| `CreateKeyspace` | `POST /` |
| `CreateTable` | `POST /` |
| `CreateType` | `POST /` |
| `DeleteKeyspace` | `POST /` |
| `DeleteTable` | `POST /` |
| `DeleteType` | `POST /` |
| `GetKeyspace` | `POST /` |
| `GetTable` | `POST /` |
| `GetType` | `POST /` |
| `ListKeyspaces` | `POST /` |
| `ListTables` | `POST /` |
| `ListTagsForResource` | `POST /` |
| `ListTypes` | `POST /` |
| `TagResource` | `POST /` |
| `UntagResource` | `POST /` |
| `UpdateKeyspace` | `POST /` |
| `UpdateTable` | `POST /` |
